task.name: CODEOWNERS Coverage Remediation
task.description: Review default-branch changes that newly leave a repository-declared sensitive path without an effective eligible CODEOWNERS owner, and surface only supported path-level gaps that are not already tracked or covered by an accepted bounded exception.
task.intent: Reduce operator time spent finding and restoring ownership for newly unowned sensitive paths while avoiding duplicate attention and treating only repository-accepted ownership restoration as attained remediation.
activationConditions: A merged default-branch change within the evidence window adds or moves a path covered by the repository's sensitive-path policy, or changes CODEOWNERS rules affecting such a path.

Authoritative default-branch content, sensitive-path policy, and CODEOWNERS last-match resolution show that the changed sensitive path has no effective owner that is currently eligible under the repository's declared ownership policy.
requiredEffects: Each novel finding identifies one canonical sensitive path or policy path pattern, the change that made it newly unowned, the sensitivity-policy basis, the effective CODEOWNERS resolution, and the eligibility evidence supporting the gap.
Each surfaced finding provides a repository-linked remediation proposal that maintainers can accept, reject, or supersede without granting the workflow direct write authority.
noopConditions: Every changed sensitive path retains at least one effective eligible CODEOWNERS owner after default-branch CODEOWNERS resolution.
Every supported newly unowned sensitive-path finding is already tracked or covered by an explicit, unexpired maintainer-accepted exception for the same path and ownership gap.
successConditions: Supported newly unowned sensitive-path findings receive accepted ownership-restoration evidence within 14 days of the workflow run.
Sensitive paths that remain effectively owned, and ownership gaps already tracked or covered by an accepted bounded exception, create no duplicate maintainer attention.
uncertainties: CODEOWNERS uses last-matching-rule semantics, so an apparently broad owner can be displaced by a later rule and must not be assumed effective.
When owner eligibility, team visibility, sensitive-path policy, or default-branch evidence cannot be read, the workflow cannot safely infer either adequate coverage or a supported ownership gap.

operationalValue.statement: The proportion of supported, novel newly unowned sensitive-path findings assigned to the run that receive repository-accepted ownership restoration within 14 days.
operationalValue.opportunity: One workflow run and the deduplicated supported newly unowned sensitive-path findings it assigns for covered default-branch changes.
acceptedEvidence: A merged pull request in the evaluated repository updates CODEOWNERS or the affected path so authoritative default-branch resolution assigns at least one effective owner that is eligible under the repository's declared ownership policy before the evidence cutoff.

A repository-linked maintainer acceptance record for a superseding ownership-remediation pull request, together with authoritative default-branch evidence that the accepted change restored effective eligible ownership for the same sensitive path before the evidence cutoff.
evidenceRepositories: The repository in which the workflow ran and whose default branch contains the evaluated sensitive path, sensitive-path policy, CODEOWNERS file, and accepted remediation.

metric.name: accepted-sensitive-path-ownership-remediations
metric.formula: supported novel newly unowned sensitive-path findings with accepted ownership-restoration evidence / supported novel newly unowned sensitive-path findings assigned to the run

operationalValue.maturation: 14 days after the workflow run completes.
operationalValue.zeroRule: Return 0 when at least one supported novel newly unowned sensitive-path finding was assigned and none has accepted ownership-restoration evidence by the evidence cutoff.
operationalValue.missingRule: Return null when the assigned finding set or required default-branch path, sensitive-path policy, CODEOWNERS resolution, owner-eligibility, or remediation-acceptance evidence cannot be read.
